Charge radiation reaction: stochastic (Poissonian E1-dipole photon kicks).
Trajectory integrator: adaptive symmetric second-order step.
Pair: electron + positron (reduced mass 0.5 m_e, Bohr radius 2 a0, binding 6.80285 eV).
Starting separation: a_n = 1 a_pair (n = 1) = 105.835 pm -- an initial condition for the classical inspiral, not a claimed energy eigenstate.
Interaction experiment: EACH particle's lab kinetic energy ~ N(0.6, 0.4) eV truncated at 0.012 eV, drawn independently, so the pair carries a net momentum and the centre of mass moves; K_CM below is the invariant derived from the two, and each trajectory is integrated in that COM frame.  (b_y,b_z) ~ N_2(0, sigma^2 I), hence b ~ Rayleigh(sigma = 60 pm), truncated by rejection at R_match/2; both dipoles isotropic.

The revolution count is what the bound observation window actually covered, NOT a count to collapse: these pairs are

No bound event yielded a finite collapse time: 2 of 2 had an observation window shorter than one Kepler orbit,
